title: CE and Principal Officials receive seasonal influenza vaccination (with photos) - info.gov.hk

analysis.time: The Chief Executive and Principal Officials received seasonal influenza vaccination on September 23, 2026. The vaccination programmes commenced on September 17, 2026.
analysis.location_and_population: Hong Kong, with a focus on the general public, including children and adolescents aged 6 months to under 18 years, adults aged 18 to 49 with chronic medical conditions, persons aged 50 or above, pregnant women, healthcare workers, and civil servants.
analysis.event: The Chief Executive, Mr John Lee, led Principal Officials in receiving seasonal influenza vaccination and urged the public to get vaccinated as early as possible to build an immunity barrier and protect health. The Government implemented SIV programmes and initiatives to promote vaccination.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: In the previous year (2025/26), more than 2.03 million doses were administered under various SIV programmes. Among children and adolescents, the SIV rate reached 64.8 per cent, a 13.1 percentage point increase compared to the average of the past three seasons. For adolescents aged 12 to under 18 years, the rate reached 61.4 per cent, a 22.6 percentage point increase compared to the past three seasons.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The Government has fully commenced SIV programmes on September 17, 2026, and implemented four optimising initiatives to encourage and offer convenience for vaccination. The vaccination rate for the target population is reported, and the Government continues to promote these programmes.

analysis.brief_en: On September 23, 2026, the Chief Executive of Hong Kong, Mr John Lee, led Principal Officials in receiving seasonal influenza vaccination, urging the public to get vaccinated early to build an immunity barrier and protect their health and that of their families. The Government has implemented various SIV programmes, including the Vaccination Subsidy Scheme, the Government Vaccination Programme, the SIV School Outreach Programme, and the Residential Care Home Vaccination Programme, to provide free or subsidised influenza vaccinations to eligible groups such as children and adolescents aged 6 months to under 18 years, adults with chronic medical conditions, persons aged 50 or above, pregnant women, and healthcare workers. In the previous year (2025/26), over 2.03 million doses were administered, with the SIV rate for children and adolescents reaching 64.8 per cent, a 13.1 percentage point increase compared to the average of the past three seasons. For adolescents aged 12 to under 18 years, the rate reached 61.4 per cent, a 22.6 percentage point increase. The Government has also introduced four optimising initiatives, including a new Electronic Consent Form and increased vaccine procurement, to enhance public access to SIV services. These efforts aim to reduce the risk of influenza transmission and hospitalisation, particularly among vulnerable groups.

title: Recommendations announced for influenza vaccine composition for the 2027 southern hemisphere influenza season - World Health Organization (WHO)

analysis.time: 25 September 2026 (publication date), 2027 southern hemisphere influenza season (event date).
analysis.location_and_population: Global, with focus on southern hemisphere countries.
analysis.event: WHO announced recommendations for the 2027 southern hemisphere influenza vaccine composition, based on international consultation and surveillance data.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: The recommendations aim to improve vaccine effectiveness against seasonal influenza viruses, including A(H1N1)pdm09, A(H3N2), and B/Victoria lineage. No specific case counts, death counts, or exposure numbers were reported.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: WHO conducted an international consultation and reviewed surveillance data from GISRS and other sources. The recommendations are based on this review and are intended for vaccine development for the upcoming season.

analysis.brief_en: The World Health Organization (WHO) announced on 25 September 2026 its recommendations for the 2027 southern hemisphere influenza vaccine composition. These recommendations were made following an international consultation involving experts from WHO's Collaborating Centres and Essential Regulatory Laboratories. The WHO Global Influenza Surveillance and Response System (GISRS) and other sources provided the surveillance data used to determine the vaccine strains. The focus of the recommendations includes seasonal influenza viruses such as A(H1N1)pdm09, A(H3N2), and B/Victoria lineage. No specific case counts, death counts, or exposure numbers were reported in the supplied evidence. The recommendations are intended to guide vaccine development for the upcoming season and emphasize the importance of global solidarity in public health efforts. The WHO's Director for Epidemic and Pandemic Management, Dr Maria Van Kerhove, highlighted the long-standing effectiveness of the GISRS in informing vaccine strategies.
